title: Genesis 1 as compressed creation report
statement: The seven-day creation account of Genesis 1 is read, per the canon's decoded reading (with Sendy's earlier literalist statement as precedent), as a compressed report of staged creation work: the 'days' as long working periods, the firmament and waters as the account's own observational vocabulary, the sequence of works as project stages culminating in the human synthesis — a report transmitted and compressed, not a cosmogony; the record carries the reading at the canon's level and keeps the mainstream literary-critical account of Genesis 1 in its own voice.

includes: The staged reading: days as periods, the works as stages, the vocabulary as observational — the decoded Genesis of the canon's opening chapter (the corpus's 'The Truth' entry is this reading's page)
The Sendy precedent: the 1963 literalist statement as the reading's modern forerunner, engaged through woh-claim-0042's convergence record
The completion joint: the account's human-creation stage hands over to the Eden record (woh-claim-0018) and the anthropogony comparison (woh-claim-0034)
excludes: Concordism with modern cosmology; the reading maps the text onto the project's stages, never onto Big Bang chronology, and prose that does the latter has left the record
The two-source question (Genesis 1 versus Genesis 2) as a target; the documentary observation is mainstream context, preserved
Day-length arithmetic; the canon reads periods, and the corpus does not compute them
Extension to the primeval history beyond the creation account; Flood and Babel have their own records

source_references.locator: Chapter 2, 'The Truth': the decoded Genesis reading, verse family by verse family

alternatives.statement: Genesis 1 is P's structured liturgical cosmology (the mainstream account); its sevens and separations are theology of order, not compressed reportage.
The account's firmament-and-waters vocabulary is shared ancient Near Eastern cosmology; reading observation into it retrofits a modern frame.
Staged readings of Genesis 1 historically slide into concordism; the framework version inherits the genre's failure mode.
